directAnswer: To set up a Git branch, use the command 'git branch <branch-name>' to create a new branch and 'git checkout <branch-name>' to switch to it.
summary: This guide provides steps to create and switch to a new Git branch, along with caveats and FAQs.

sections.heading: Creating a Git Branch
sections.body: You can create a new branch in your local repository using the command line.

sections.heading: Switching to a New Branch
sections.body: After creating a branch, you can switch to it using Git commands to start working on it.

sections.heading: Merging Branches
sections.body: Once your work is complete, you can merge your branch back into the main branch.

steps.title: Open Terminal or Command Prompt
steps.detail: Navigate to your Git repository using the terminal or command prompt.

steps.title: Create a New Branch
steps.detail: Run the command 'git branch <branch-name>' to create a new branch.

steps.title: Switch to the New Branch
steps.detail: Use 'git checkout <branch-name>' to switch to the newly created branch.

steps.title: Merge the Branch (Optional)
steps.detail: To merge your branch into the main branch, switch back to the main branch and run 'git merge <branch-name>'.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 'git branch' and 'git checkout'?
faqs.answer: 'git branch' creates a new branch, while 'git checkout' switches to an existing branch.

faqs.question: Can I create a branch from a specific commit?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can create a branch from a specific commit using 'git branch <branch-name> <commit-hash>'.

faqs.question: How do I delete a branch?
faqs.answer: You can delete a branch using 'git branch -d <branch-name>' if it's fully merged, or 'git branch -D <branch-name>' to force delete.

caveats: Ensure you have committed any changes before switching branches to avoid losing work.
Branch names must be unique within the repository.
